“Good Friday” is the day on which Christ was crucified. The “Good” in the English phrase “Good Friday” comes from an archaic meaning of the wordGood—“Holy.” In Spanish, “Good Friday” is “Viernes Santo” and in French, “Le Vendredi saint,” both of which translate into English as “Holy Friday.” Thus, when we think of Good Friday, we can think of “Holy Friday,” or “Sacred Friday,” or, as Elder Jeffrey R. Holland of the Quorum of the Twelve Apostles phrased it, “atoning Friday with its cross” (“None Were with Him,”EnsignorLiahona,May 2009, 88).
